title: Calibration observables, allowed/forbidden substitutions, and cohomological alignment
html:
ID Canonical observable canonical proxy What it fixes DOF of H^1 = 2W
CAL-1 m_\mathfrak{e} (leptonic mass scale, order h^0) electron mass (Penning trap) the dimensional unit W-plane scale
CAL-2 P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta} (neutron \beta-sector bar-skew channel, order h^2) \mathfrak{Q}_\beta = P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta}; the modulus is overdetermined, pinned most precisely by m_\mu/m_\mathfrak{e} = \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\hbar_q^2, \hbar_q = 1-q_0^{-1} substrate q_0 W-plane modulus
CAL-3 P_{\mathrm{avg}}^{\pi} (pion-sector bar-even channel, order h^3) charged-pion mass m_\pi (PDG); independent of (m_\mathfrak{e}, q_0) via \mathrm{Vol}(\mathrm{Hopf})=0 meson scale orthogonal class

All three are the three real degrees of freedom of the single H^1 = 2W (rank-2 W-plane scale + modulus, plus one orthogonal class: 2+1=3), not three distinct degrees H^0/H^1/H^2.

The three canonical inputs are weak-sector observables — a leptonic mass scale and two bar-parity channels (m_\mathfrak{e}, P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta}, P_{\mathrm{avg}}^{\pi}), entering at successive orders h^0, h^2, h^3. They are read off their most precisely measured proxies — the masses m_\mathfrak{e}, m_\pi and the Q-value \mathfrak{Q}_\beta = \hbar/P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta}. m_\mathfrak{e} sets the unit, so the (dimensionless) modulus q_0 is pinned by the ratio m_\mu/m_\mathfrak{e} — the most precise anchor for CAL-2.

\mathfrak{Q}_\beta is the measured proxy for CAL-2 (P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta}), the bar-odd \sinh partner of the bar-even \cosh meson scale m_\pi; it is not a fourth calibration. Because the modulus is overdetermined, \mathfrak{Q}_\beta and the lepton ratio m_\mu/m_\mathfrak{e} are alternative handles on the same CAL-2 — whichever is used to pin q_0, the other becomes a cross-check prediction. In the Physical-Observations layer q_0 may instead be anchored on the more-precise proton ratio m_p/m_\mathfrak{e} (the muon ratio is then a 9.5\sigma cross-check), a precision substitution within the same H^1 datum — not a fourth calibration.

The three inputs are independent: one dimensionless ratio plus two dimensional scales. They align to the three (co)homological degrees of freedom that survive on-shell quotient by \star_q F_\nabla = F_\nabla and gauge invariance \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0 — namely the three Wedderburn blocks (sym, std, alt) of H_3(R, q) (three parameters from Wedderburn).

Allowed substitutions

  • q_0 is a canonical constant only via CAL-2; downstream compute must carry q_0 symbolically as long as possible and substitute the CAL-2 exact algebraic values at the final reporting step.
  • \mathfrak{E}_0 has two framework-derived forms and one CODATA cross-check, all related by the brane-tower correction 1/(1-\hbar_q^2):
    • \mathfrak{E}_0^{(N=0)} = m_e/(q_0(q_0-1)) \approx 4.186 MeV (single Planck-tick, CAL-1 + CAL-2 only),
    • \mathfrak{E}_0^{\text{full}} = \mathfrak{E}_0^{(N=0)}/(1-\hbar_q^2) \approx 4.228 MeV (tower-summed, CAL-1 + CAL-2 only),
    • \mathfrak{E}_0^{(\text{cal})} = \mathfrak{Q}_\beta(n)/|\Delta(\mathrm{net})| \approx 4.155 MeV (CAL-3 cross-check via CODATA). See the notation register energy row and the collisions note for the convention \mathfrak{E}_0 \neq \mathfrak{Q}_\beta(n) (they differ by the dimensionless factor 1/|\Delta(\mathrm{net})| \approx 5.31).
  • m_e enters as the unique dimensional bridge from \mathbb{Q}(q_0) to MeV.

Forbidden substitutions

The framework forbids:

  • Free parameters beyond CAL-1, CAL-2, CAL-3.
  • Coefficient fits to AME, CODATA, PDG, or any external dataset (e.g. "ad hoc" or "approx" tags on Bethe-Weizsäcker coefficients must be derived to symbolic \mathbb{Q}(q_0) form, not retained as fits).
  • Numerological substitutions (e.g. magic numbers \{2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126\} asserted as data; they must be derived from Bring's surface period structure or the BB / LR homological framework).
  • A second pinning of q_0. The substrate uncertainty floor \delta q_0 propagated from CODATA m_\mu/m_e is a CAL-2 cross-check; it may not be supplemented by independent fits to m_e, m_\mu, m_\tau, or any other mass.
  • A second hadronic scale. m_{\pi^{\pm}} is the CAL-3 proxy; the hadronic energy scale \mathfrak{E}_0 is derived from CAL-1 + CAL-2, and \mathfrak{Q}_\beta(n) is the CAL-2 proxy — neither is an independent fourth input. Proton mass, neutron mass, and all nuclear binding energies must be derived from \{m_e, q_0, m_{\pi^{\pm}}\}, not introduced as inputs.

(Co)homological alignment

The Wedderburn-Artin decomposition H_3(R, q) \cong M_1^{\mathrm{sym}} \oplus M_2^{\mathrm{std}} \oplus M_1^{\mathrm{alt}} gives three independent block characters \chi_\lambda for \lambda \in \{(3), (2,1), (1^3)\}, with degrees 1, 2, 1. The three on-shell parameters of the categorical action survive as the three independent traces \mathrm{tr}_\lambda, one per block.

The calibration map is:

Wedderburn block Calibration Role
\mathrm{alt} (\lambda = (1^3)) CAL-2: P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta} (proxy m_\mu/m_e) \mapsto q_0 Sets the deformation scale (alt is the "antisymmetric" / antimatter channel; q_0 = 1 collapses it).
\mathrm{std} (\lambda = (2,1)) CAL-1: m_e Sets the leptonic mass quantum (std is the 2-dimensional "matter" channel where \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i\sigma_j) = z^2).
\mathrm{sym} (\lambda = (3)) CAL-3: P_{\mathrm{avg}}^{\pi} (proxy m_{\pi^{\pm}}) Sets the chiral / Goldstone scale (sym is the "all crossings positive" / hadronic channel). The pion mass is the pseudo-Goldstone boson of broken chiral \mathrm{SU}(2)_A; its mass encodes the chiral condensate \langle\bar{q}q\rangle^{1/3} \approx 240\;\mathrm{MeV} which is absent from (m_e, q_0). \mathfrak{Q}_\beta(n) is the measured proxy for CAL-2 (P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta}); when q_0 is pinned by the alternative anchor m_\mu/m_e, the relation \mathfrak{Q}_\beta = m_e \lvert q_0^2 - 2q_0 - 1\rvert(q_0+1)/(2q_0^3) \approx 0.784\;\mathrm{MeV} (0.17% miss) makes it a cross-check on the same modulus, not a fourth input.

This is the meaning of "aligned to (co)homology": the three calibrations correspond bijectively to the three irreducible characters of H_3(R, q), which are the three cohomology classes that survive the on-shell / gauge-invariance quotient. The framework is rigid in this sense: increasing or decreasing the number of calibrations would require deforming the categorical substrate to a different on-shell quotient, which would no longer satisfy the QOU axioms.

Comparison with the Standard Model

The Standard Model has 19 free parameters (6 quark masses, 3 lepton masses, 3 CKM angles + 1 phase, 3 gauge couplings, Higgs mass, Higgs VEV, QCD theta angle). The QOU framework replaces all 19 with these 3 (calibration inputs context):

  • particle content is topological (from \chi(A) = -6), not chosen;
  • mass ratios are knot invariants (from algebraic quantum volume and \mathrm{tr}_M), not free;
  • coupling constants are R-matrix eigenvalues (from q_0);
  • mixing angles are Clebsch-Gordan coefficients of the knot eigenbasis decomposition.

The 19 \to 3 reduction forms a testable claim. Any prediction requiring a fourth calibration falsifies the framework.
